properties.statement:
① SYMPTOM (Alex, v0.47.0, 2026-09-05): add_epoch requires `sequence` on create, but the refusal cannot say what value to pass; the caller learns it (max existing + 1) only by separately scanning epochs. ② PRECEDENT: none for the refusal; but chg:the-philosophy-epoch-makes-room-for-a-cut (a planned epoch moved 360 -> 365 so a release cut could take the sequence it actually happened at) shows sequences are deliberately SPACED and re-ordered — they carry meaning, not just order.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) the refusal is produced by the generic RequiredFields helper (service.rs), which knows the field is missing and nothing about epochs, so it cannot compute a hint; (b) sequence could be optional and auto-assigned; (c) the schema should not require it at all. ④⑤ MEASURED: the add_epoch handler calls `__rf.i64("sequence", req.sequence)` then `__rf.finish()` — the same helper that produced the observed refusal '`name` is required to CREATE ChangeEvent ... pass `name`' in this session. The helper's text is type-agnostic by construction. (a) is the mechanism. (b) and (c) are design questions, not causes — recorded as dec:idea-add-epoch-assigns-the-next-sequence-or-names-it (brainstorm, Alex's idea).

⑥ CLASS: a generic refusal at the point where a type-specific hint is one cheap read away. The description-redirect on add_change_event (#429) is the same shape and the same fix: a pre-check in the handler, before the generic helper, that says what WOULD have worked. Here: 'sequence is required; the highest existing is N, so N+1 (or any larger value — sequences are spaced on purpose) would place this after everything.' ⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether auto-assigning is right at all — that is the brainstorm.

═══ RECURRENCE #2, 2026-09-06, ON THE SIBLING ═══ plan_epoch (shipped in v0.49.0 as the planned form of add_epoch) gave the SAME generic refusal — "`sequence` is required to CREATE DesignEpoch … pass `sequence`" — and the caller (the reflow2 session itself, planning an increment) found the maximum by scanning the export by hand. The hint Alex's fix put on add_epoch did not reach the sibling: the class in ⑥ recurred because the fix was placed in one handler rather than where both share. Counted here under rule:every-failure-is-searched-and-every-cause-is-root-caused-before-it-is-written (tier 1: the search found this record); the fix is to share the pre-check between the two constructors, taken in the v0.50.0 item-3 change.
